correctness.rationale: The only possible nonzero products of distinct positive root units occur on directed two-step paths, with no cancellation in any characteristic. The source and target sets of a commuting arc family are disjoint, so unused vertices can be assigned to a cut with 1 on the source side and n on the sink side. For an arc outside this cut, composing it with 1->a or b->n (whichever endpoint has the wrong cut side) prevents adding it. These endpoint arcs also determine the cut uniquely. If x_i is an interior source bit, the columns include 1, x_i and x_i(1-x_j), and the remaining endpoint columns are 1-x_j. In the integral span, x_i(1-x_j) is interchangeable with x_ix_j using x_i. On the rows of support at most two the resulting inclusion evaluation matrix is unit triangular; these column operations on the chosen square submatrix give a genuine unit minor. This proves both rank and all unit Smith factors. The all-subsets alternating vectors form a unit triangular basis and their pairings with the monomial x_H are exactly delta_{J,H}; the high-degree vectors therefore give the full integral kernel, not merely a sublattice. The Walsh basis gives the same rational complement, and positive semidefiniteness identifies the Gram kernel over Q. The first nonzero mode has |J|=3, hence n=5. The size formula subtracts sink-before-source pairs in the middle binary word from s(n-s); the n-1 compulsory endpoint arcs are the whole cut precisely when the interior sinks precede the interior sources, yielding n-1 minima. An initial balanced source segment attains the upper bound. This covers n=2,3,4 with a zero kernel; no claim concerns the Gram kernel in small positive characteristic or arbitrary abelian subalgebras. The supplied finite checker was inspected, not executed; in particular its modular ranks are not a Smith certificate.

originality.rationale: The distinct claim is the integral and rational reconstruction theorem for the labeled root incidence operator, including the kernel in the original clique coordinates. The source/sink paradigm and the low-degree Boolean tools are established, as is the equivalent generic pairwise marginal operator. Neither the inspected root-cut classifications nor the prior marginal model states or supplies the identification of individual positive-root incidences with the full marginal data on the anchored cuts. I credit the generic tools and cut precedent, not an independent discovery of them. The exact size census is an elementary secondary corollary, not the basis for passing originality.
residual_risks: Earlier shift-graph incidence or design terminology could cover the identification more directly than sources found in the bounded lookup.
Two plausible upper-triangular subalgebra papers could not be read in full; their access limits alone do not affect the binary conclusion.

value.rationale: The root-incidence operator answers a concrete reconstruction problem on distributions of naturally defined maximal commuting supports. It identifies every detectable interaction, gives a complete integral basis in the original support coordinates for all invisible differences, locates the first failure at n=5, and rules out torsion obstructions. The applicability of standard margin and Walsh methods to this specific directed-root data is the useful structure; a standalone Gaussian size identity or the abstract orthogonality of Walsh modes would not suffice.
